messages:
alex: Hit a new repro on the mac sample app when switching networks (WiFi -> hotspot). Streaming SSE returns a partial final chunk twice and parser errors with "duplicate-trailer-token".

alex: Steps: start sample app streaming; flip network quickly; reconnect happens automatically; logs show tail fragment replayed and then [DONE] again.

jamie: Can you paste the raw receive log around reconnect?

alex: small snippet:
```
[2026-04-03T08:12:01Z] RECV: data: {"id":"r1","text":"last-part"}
[2026-04-03T08:12:02Z] NET: connection reset (network switch)
[2026-04-03T08:12:02.500Z] RECONNECT
[2026-04-03T08:12:02.510Z] RECV: data: {"id":"r1","text":"last-part"}
[2026-04-03T08:12:02.511Z] RECV: data: [DONE]
[2026-04-03T08:12:02.512Z] PARSER: error duplicate-trailer-token
```

lee: Sounds like client-side reconnect logic replays in-flight buffered fragments. Node/Python differ: python uses last-event-id dedupe, node historically replays.

alex: This repro is on Swift sample app. Likely parity issue in reconnect path. Quick mitigation: ignore duplicate [DONE] for same id within 3s window.

jamie: Agree. Add telemetry counter client.duplicate_trailer_count and a unit test that simulates fast net-switch plus reconnect. Also add a note to onboarding: "Mobile/net-change can cause stream tail replay; SDKs should handle duplicate trailers gracefully."

devops-bot: Created issue INF-1842 to track SDK parity and reconciler for reconnect semantics.

lee: Long-term: converge on sequence numbers/last-event-id across SDKs. Short-term patch + tests OK.

alex: Will open PR with 3s ignore-window + metric and test. Thanks!
